messages:
Emma: heads-up — customer (org: org-8421) says their monthly credits hit 0 last night and then jumped back up ~03:15 local time. They saw quota_exceeded errors for ~2h, then UI showed full refill earlier than their expected reset. They want to know whether this is DST / timezone bug or a real double-refill. Screenshot: https://files.internal/shot.png
Carlos (oncall): can you paste the org id + sample request ids for the 429s? also which deployment (hosted/dedicated/private)?
Emma: org-8421, sample request id: rq_0a9c8f, another: rq_0a9c9. Hosted API. Customer timezone = Europe/Berlin (CEST currently).
usage-bot: monthly_usage_summary org=org-8421 tokens_consumed=1,092,430 credits_remaining=0 reset_window=2026-04-01T00:00:00Z refill_job_status=success shard=5
Sanjay (backend): quick notes/questions: 1) backend refill job always runs at 00:00:00Z (UTC) for monthly cycles. 2) UI displays reset time converted to tenant timezone — if conversion/display is wrong it can look like "early" refill. 3) need to check cache TTL on credits key and DB write timestamp. can you share the exact times the customer saw 0 vs when they saw it refill?
Emma: customer says saw 0 at 2026-03-31 23:45 CEST, then saw refill at 2026-04-01 03:15 CEST. Converted to UTC that's 2026-03-31 21:45Z -> 2026-04-01 01:15Z. Backend logs I grabbed: ``
2026-04-01T00:00:00Z INFO refill_job shard=5 start
2026-04-01T00:00:02Z INFO refill_job shard=5 org=org-8421 credits_before=0 credits_after=1000000 write_latency_ms=42
2026-04-01T00:00:03Z INFO cache_invalidate key=credits:org-8421 ttl_old=10800
``
Noor (billing): as Sanjay said, refill job succeeded at 00:00Z for that org. The cache_invalidate log is interesting — ttl_old=10800s (3h). if the UI reads from cache the client could see stale 0 until cache TTL expired or explicit invalidation propagated. DST shouldn't affect backend refill time (always UTC).
Sanjay (backend): repro steps for support to run against the org: ```bash
# check credits header from internal API
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/org-8421/credits" -i
# check usage to confirm tokens consumed
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/org-8421/usage?month=2026-03" -i
```
Look for headers: `X-Credits-Remaining`, `X-Credits-Reset-At`. Example header we saw: `X-Credits-Remaining: 1000000`, `X-Credits-Reset-At: 2026-04-01T00:00:00Z`. If UI shows a different reset time, screenshot the network panel.
Emma: customer also got quota_exceeded 429s with body: { "error": "quota_exceeded", "remaining": 0 } then later requests succeeded. They reported the UI indicated reset at 01:00 local which caused confusion. I told them we were investigating cache/display alignment.
Carlos (oncall): recommended immediate customer reply: 1) confirm refill occurs at 00:00 UTC, 2) explain UI shows times in tenant timezone and we discovered a cache TTL that can delay visible update (we'll fix), 3) offer manual top-up if they need immediate capacity. Also open a bug/incident to track fix.
Sanjay (backend): root cause proposal: refill job writes DB at 00:00Z and triggers cache invalidation, but some cache nodes kept a 3h TTL fallback (10800s) for credits keys; UI reads cached value until TTL expires causing a visible lag between backend state and UI. Action items: - Reduce credits cache TTL to 30s for next deploy. - Add immediate cache eviction after refill (ensure distributed invalidation). - Add metric: credits_cache_stale_count and alert if >0 for >5m after refill. - Postmortem/INC: INC-2026-432 assigned to eng-infra + billing.
Noor (billing): I'll schedule a one-time reconciliation for any orgs that saw discrepancy and prepare customer-friendly wording for billing team.
Emma: response to customer drafted: "Refill runs at 00:00 UTC. We found a caching edge that can delay the UI update by up to 3 hours; your credits were actually refilled at 00:00 UTC and were usable, but the dashboard showed 0 until cache expired. We're rolling a fix (reduce TTL + immediate eviction) and will follow up when the deploy is live. If you need immediate tokens we can do a manual top-up now. Sorry for the confusion :pray:"
Carlos (oncall): thumbs up. please add screenshots/network trace if customer can provide it. I'll track the incident until mitigation is deployed.
Emma: closing notes — customer accepted manual top-up while we push the fix, asked for ETA ~24h. I added them to the incident notification list. Will update thread when deploy completes. :white_check_mark:
